b.x: What it is, in the craft

To visualize, here, is not a wish-board on the wall. It is not the universe delivering a car. It is rehearsal: the brain walks the gesture before the street. An athlete does it. A firefighter does it. Whoever evacuates a child on paper already did. The gray man does the same without putting a uniform on the thought.

Whoever only sees the end — the house saved, the hero, the light — trains the stage. Whoever sees the middle — the key, the shoe, the short sentence, the water — trains the craft. Performance science calls this process visualization. The result comes later, if it comes. The gesture comes now.
DO
Field question: am I seeing what my hands do — or the applause after? If it is applause, wipe it. Return to the hand.
Five techniques that fit a Tuesday

1. The path. Sit. Close the eye ninety seconds. Leave the bed. Key. Shoe. Door. Point B. No hero. The rail, the hall smell, the bag’s weight. Open the eye. If the gesture did not fit, the plan on paper does not fit either.

2. The twelve seconds. The street interview. Someone asks the time. You see the short sentence, the step toward light, people, emergency numbers on the tongue. You do not see the fight. You do not see the ‘disarm’. You see the no and the movement. The second-yes field.

3. The house in the dark. Three minutes. Power dies. You find the torch where it already is. Water. Radio. The child by name, not by shout. A foot on known ground. Whoever never rehearsed this in the light will rehearse it in the black — worse.

4. The tone. Before the street: one minute of gratitude in the body — chest, shoulder, mouth. Not a stage mantra. Data. Then open the eye on Tuesday. Fields 23 and 94: fear contracts; a high tone does not erase the fact — it holds the hand for the fact.

5. The non-hero. Visualize being what the street does not pick. Clothes of the block. The pace of someone who lives there. No chest. No kit on the shoulder. The scene ends and nobody recounts you. That is expansion of consciousness on the asphalt — not a story lamp.
Five senses, one gesture

A weak image does not enter the body. Rehearsal asks for sense: what you see, what you hear, what the foot feels, the hall smell, the dry taste in the mouth if the body tightens. One sense at a time, then join them. Ninety seconds. If the head turns into a film, cut. Return to the foot.
NOTE
Child: a short true rehearsal. ‘Lights out. We find the torch. Your name.’ No end-of-world film. Their body reads yours — field 93.
Three minutes, no altar
01 Sit. Foot on the floor. Three breaths. Field 93: name the tone.
02 Pick one rehearsal: path, twelve seconds, house in the dark, tone, non-hero.
03 Ninety seconds of process. Hand, not applause.
04 Open the eye. One Tuesday action: torch in place, a sentence in the pocket, water in the pantry.
You do not need music. You do not need a group. You do not need 21 days on a story. One rehearsal the house already eats is worth more than an hour at an altar.
What this field refuses
It does not teach a vision board, shop-window attraction, ‘asking the universe’ in place of water.
It does not teach seeing the fight and winning. It teaches seeing the no and leaving.
It does not replace rehearsal with the body: the torch exists or it does not. The child’s sheet exists or it does not.
It does not replace a doctor, emergency care. Panic, flashback, despair: the clinic, not the closed eye.
It teaches only this: the closed eye trains the hand. The hand trains Tuesday. Tuesday is the test. Field 94 gives the tone. This field gives the gesture.
